statements.statement: Executive director (Renee)
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said she approves new things for now and she is the one site directors report to.

statements.statement: We want AI to take paperwork and planning off your plate. We must protect the children... keep our promise to the district.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches the hopes (activity plans, paperwork) and the worry about student data and the district agreement.

statements.statement: Staff, group leaders, volunteers, contractors and board members.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call named no exceptions; this is the template's general coverage.

statements.statement: tools: [] (No AI tool is approved yet.)
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said they bought nothing and no leader approved any tool, so an empty list is correct.

statements.statement: Renee approves any new tool, plugin or AI feature in existing software.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said she says yes to new things for now.

statements.statement: Joy checks the settings first.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said Joy handles systems and would check settings.

statements.statement: If student data is involved, the district must agree too.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said the district must agree for anything with student data.

statements.statement: Use a work account where we have one, and turn off any setting that lets the vendor train...
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call is silent; this is the template's default accounts line.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Everyone, now: any AI tool, through a work email, for work with no information about a real person in it.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call settled nothing and did not say no to this, so the template default applies.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Group leaders: activity ideas, STEM projects and games.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Group leaders described exactly this use.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Site directors: schedules and weekly reports with no child or family details.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Site directors want help with schedules and weekly reports; the no-details limit fits everyone-now.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Site directors: drafting the weekly parent newsletter.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Sam uses AI to write the weekly parent newsletter.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Translating the newsletter into Spanish and Vietnamese.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Sam translates the newsletter into both languages.

statements.statement: Grant reports or outcomes data for the state or funders — Executive director (Renee)
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: Renee was named as approver for new things, not for this use; the call named no approver for grant reports, so use the default, your manager. Also the grant writer question is still open.

statements.statement: AI-drafted messages to parents beyond the weekly newsletter — Your manager
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call flagged parent notes as risky without naming an approver, so the default approver applies.

statements.statement: Children's names, photos and video, grades and test scores, attendance, IEP and 504 information, allergies and medications, custody and pickup orders, and behavior incident reports.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: All listed by Renee on the call.

statements.statement: Also donor names and contact details, staff and volunteer information, and all passwords and logins.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Donor list was mentioned; staff info and passwords are template defaults.

statements.statement: Our district data-sharing agreement keeps student records in the district platform.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee described this agreement.

statements.statement: Never put an incident report, or a note about a child's behavior, into AI, even to clean it up.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee's worry about pasting incident reports in to clean them up, and notes about behavior are legal-type documents.

statements.statement: Never use AI for mandated reporting. If you suspect abuse, call it in yourself.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said this never goes near AI.

statements.statement: Never make AI images of our kids, or use AI to edit photos of real kids.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said no to both.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: Whoever sends AI-assisted work is responsible for it. Check facts, names, numbers, dates and tone first.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default review line.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: Check every pickup time and date in a translated newsletter. Grant report numbers must match our records.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Follows from Sam's pickup-time example and Renee's point that grant outcomes must be right.

statements.statement: AI never decides a child's placement, discipline, accommodations or pickup, or who we hire.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default; the call did not discuss these decisions.

statements.statement: AI never sees a child's information.
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: Contradicts the stated rule that tools may hold no protected information, but also overstates: fine as policy, yet the line was meant for what AI may do to support deciders; rephrase to what AI may do.

statements.statement: Machine-translated newsletters say so, so parents know to ask if something looks wrong.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee asked for this.

statements.statement: We will tell parents before AI is used with their children in our program.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee said parents would want to know if kids use a chatbot in the program.

statements.statement: Tell your site director the same day. Site directors tell Renee the same day.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Sam said this directly.

statements.statement: Reporting a mistake... is expected and never punished.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default.

statements.statement: Renee owns this policy day to day and shares it with all staff and volunteers.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee is the owner; sharing with staff is the template default.

statements.statement: Joy checks tool settings. We review this policy in 12 months.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Joy checking settings is from the call; 12 months is the template default.

statements.statement: Do children use AI during homework hour, and do we follow each school's rule or make our own? (Board and principals)
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee left this open and said it needs the board and principals.

statements.statement: Will the board approve and pay for any AI tool, such as Gemini in Google Workspace or ChatGPT?
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call left tool approval unsettled; these tools were named.

statements.statement: How will we learn how our grant writer uses AI, and what must they follow?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Renee assumes the contractor uses AI and never asked.

statements.statement: Who will check the Vietnamese translation of the newsletter before it goes out?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Sam said nobody checks the Vietnamese.

missed: Group leaders' unofficial use of ChatGPT and personal phones is not addressed beyond the default.
Translating the newsletter is allowed under everyone-now, but the Vietnamese check is unsettled, so the allowed use sits uneasily with the open question.
Renee's worry about a photo of a child's homework with a name being put into ChatGPT is not named as a specific example.
The state monitor asking for an AI policy is not mentioned.
Parent volunteer checks the Spanish translation but that is not stated.
Students using their own phones or school Chromebooks for homework help is not described in the policy.
